Part I — Knowledge Base (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Knowledge Base (Session 69, English)
The Third Eye Batch: The 1 1-Day Sadhna, Specialization, Astral-W orld Rules, and Bhaiya's Own Journey Into a Tantrik-Bound Family's Home

Sour ce: a live Ashaeiynn session specifically for a new "Thir d Eye" batch, opening with the induction/enr ollment of new members into an 1 1-day intensive sadhna, followed by a set of advanced teachings not normally shar ed publicly (specialization/vidya acquisition, self-healing limitations, and four specific "astral world rules"), an unusually candid and personally vulnerable account fr om Bhaiya of his own frightening astral journey the pr evious night, and a closing practical Q&A on the 1 1-day sadhna's rules. This session contains extensive live interaction — enr ollment confirmations, a lar ge r oll call, and detailed practical Q&A — so it is pr ocessed as a full 3-part document.
1. Session Context: Enr ollment Into the 1 1-Day Sadhna

This session opens with practitioners confirming enrollment into an 1 1-day sadhna , explicitly framed as a prerequisite stage — after completing it, further secret sadhnas become available, and those specifically granted permission will be allowed to perform havan . Bhaiya notes that as people naturally drop out of the practice over time, the group's focus shifts to newly enrolled members, and only those who have watched a specific prior orientation video are formally enrolled via sankalp (vow).
2. What This Session's Teaching Level Repr esents

Bhaiya explicitly states that this session covers material he does not share with everyone — comparing general practice to completing a graduation and master's degree, with this level representing specialization : the stage where each practitioner begins to discover their own unique elemental/vidya specialization as they continue practicing, rather than a single generic path applying to all.
3. Specialization and the Range of Available Vidyas

As practitioners continue their sadhna, they gradually and individually gain access to dif ferent specialized vidyas (esoteric techniques/powers), including: cell repairing (the ability to repair/heal at a cellular level, similar to traditional folk "jhaada" healing rituals used against specific illnesses like TB or malaria), transpar ency/trikaal drishti (the ability to see past, present, and future), mind-reading , agni vidya (fire-based technique), ashwini vidya , and sanjivani vidya — each explored gradually , one at a time, as a practitioner's sadhna deepens.
4. No One Specializes in Everything — But Coordination Fills the Gap

Bhaiya is explicit that no single practitioner can specialize in every vidya. However , just as someone with a PhD can network with other PhD holders, practitioners with dif ferent specializations can coordinate and support one another (through the help of sants and other advanced practitioners) to collectively address any need — this coordination, not individual omniscience, is how the wider group is able to address a very broad range of problems.
5. The Central Paradox: You Can Heal Others, But Rar ely Yourself

Per this teaching, mastering a healing/repair vidya typically does not extend to one's own body or one's own family . Bhaiya illustrates this with two examples: a young girl ("Akshara") who had under gone a harmful maaran kriya (a black-magic ritual) and fallen into what looked like a coma, with 25 "pret" (spirits) reportedly occupying dif ferent parts of her body — when Baba removed them, she immediately stood up but had lost her conscious/subconscious memory , and Baba healed her fully within three days. By contrast, when a fellow practitioner ("Ankur Bhaiya") himself was injured and his own subconscious was similarly wiped, it took three months to heal, because a healer typically cannot restore their own tattva as directly as they can restore someone else's. Historical examples given: Sant Kabir ji and Tulsidas ji are described as having healed vast numbers of people through practices like reciting Ram-naam over water poured on the sick — yet neither could cure their own ailments or their own family's.
6. Why Self-Healing Doesn't Work the Same Way: Pitru vs. Purva Janam Shakti

This teaching explains the underlying mechanism: when a practitioner invokes shakti, their own pitru (ancestral spirits) are drawn toward that invoked ener gy — but pitru have no authority over a practitioner's own invoked shakti. That authority belongs specifically to the practitioner's purva janam (past-life) shakti , which has no direct relationship to the pitru lineage (the practitioner is connected to their pitru only by circumstance/karmic debt repayment, not by shared past-life shakti). Consequently , the practitioner's invoked shakti does not work on people connected to them purely through the pitru relationship — which is of fered as part of the explanation for why healers often cannot heal their own close family .
7. Astral World Rule One: No Single Mantra Works Identically for Everyone

Per this teaching, "the five fingers are not equal" — a single mantra will never work identically on every person, but for every person, there is always some mantra that will work for them specifically . Bhaiya notes this individualized-mantra-matching teaching will be covered in more depth in a future session.
8. Astral World Rule Two: Only Your Own Kundalini Shakti and Mahasookshma Sharir Protect You Fr om Cosmic Entanglement

If a practitioner becomes entangled in any brahmandiya (cosmic) ener gy , only their own kundalini shakti and their own mahasookshma sharir can protect them at that point — not even one's own Gurudev or the guru tattva itself can substitute for this at that stage.
9. Astral World Rule Three: Invoking Shakti Transfers Authority Over Your Own Body

Once a practitioner invokes their kundalini shakti or their purva janam shakti for a task, authority over their own physical body transfers to those shakti — the practitioner's body is then controlled by those forces rather than by the practitioner themself. This is described as a genuine form of freedom: freedom from bodily anxieties like vitamin D deficiency , liver problems, kidney problems, heart attack risk, or cholesterol concerns, since the practitioner's body is no longer fully "theirs" to be harmed by ordinary causes (comparable to accounts of saints like Neem Karoli Baba being unaf fected by what they eat). This teaching carries an explicit caution: this protection depends on the practitioner remaining genuinely useful to those invoked forces — if a practitioner becomes "useless," even nectar (amrit) will not help them; practitioners are ur ged to prioritize keeping these invoked shaktis "happy" over worrying about their own body .
10. Astral World Rule Four: Sincer e Intentions Manifest Fully — Including Curses

Per this teaching, once these shaktis are invoked for a task, whatever a practitioner genuinely , deeply wills in their heart will come to pass — regardless of whether it is ethical or unethical. Examples given include romantic longing eventually resolving in the practitioner's favor , unfinished tasks eventually completing, and — as a serious caution — that disrespect shown to an advanced practitioner can result in real consequences for the of fender , since such a practitioner's sincere ill will (even unintended) can manifest as genuine harm. Bhaiya references one specific real incident where an unintentional curse ("baddua") he expressed came true, of fered as
a serious caution for practitioners at this level to be very careful in what they say , rather than as something he actively wishes upon anyone.
1 1. Why Advanced Practitioners' Struggles Are Specifically Astral, Not Physical or Psychological

Per this teaching, once a practitioner reaches this level, their dif ficulties come specifically from the astral world , not from the physical world — meaning the ordinary psychological or physical complaints common to most people (headaches, stomach issues, and similar) are no longer part of their experience in the same way . This shift also changes how such a practitioner perceives others' suf fering — seeing it in terms of what is happening within a person's subtle body rather than through ordinary sympathy alone.
12. The "Ask for Others, Not Yourself" Principle and Its Reward

Bhaiya illustrates this with his own story: early on, when his own drishti (spiritual sight) had not yet opened and a fellow practitioner (Udit) asked Bhaiya to help open his own drishti, Bhaiya initially wept, telling Baba he didn't even have drishti himself to give. He then specifically prayed only that anyone who came to him would have their own drishti opened — not that he himself would receive it. That same evening, his own drishti opened as well, and it has functioned ever since (" मुझे िदखे ना िदखे सामन े वाला देख कर ही जाता है" — whether or not I see it myself, whoever comes to me leaves having seen it). This is described as an unrevokable vardaan (boon) specific to Ashaeiynn: praying for others rather than for oneself tends to result in receiving the same gift as well.
13. Never Offer Help Unprompted

Per this teaching, a practitioner should never proactively go and of fer help to someone. Help should only be given once a person comes to the practitioner and genuinely , desperately pleads for it (" िगड़िगड़ाए ")— only then should the practitioner place a hand on their head and guide them. Practicing this way ensures that only the people genuinely meant to come to a given practitioner will actually come, since their own path will bring the right people at the right time.
14. Bhaiya's Own Astral Journey , Part One: A Realm of Deceased Childr en

Bhaiya shares an unusually candid, personally dif ficult account from the previous night's dhyan, noting that he does not normally share such things this openly online but chooses to for this specific Third Eye batch. He describes being sent by Baba into a realm associated with children who died young, along with mothers who had died alongside them. He found the experience deeply disturbing and repeatedly tried to look away , but felt compelled/made to keep witnessing it, eventually forcing himself to disengage.
15. Bhaiya's Own Astral Journey , Part Two: The Gatekeepers

Later, during his own personal sadhna (done alone, just as practitioners are instructed to do), Bhaiya describes falling asleep from exhaustion mid-practice, then being woken by a sant who physically nudged/kicked him and told him it was "time to go" — a phrase that momentarily frightened him into thinking it meant death. He was told to proceed alone, and upon closing his eyes found himself at a worn, aged threshold guarded by two elderly gatekeepers (dwarpal), casually smoking bidis, who questioned him directly: "त ेर े प ास ऐ स ा क्य ा ह ै?" ("what do you actually have?"). Bhaiya answered honestly that he had nothing of his own — only guru kripa (his guru's grace) — and was allowed through, though the gatekeepers appeared unsatisfied with this answer .
16. Bhaiya's Own Astral Journey , Part Three: The Grieving Family and the Portal

Bhaiya was led to a South Indian-style home where a grieving family — a husband, his wife, the husband's younger brother , and two small children — begged him directly to come inside and help. Inside the bedroom, Bhaiya saw a fully-formed astral-world portal built directly into a blue-colored wall and ceiling, with water flowing across it and a mountain visible beyond — and realized the family itself had constructed this connection through their own rituals and sacrifices (" बिलयां दी", of ferings/sacrifices made), forming a direct link to the very same realm of deceased children Bhaiya had witnessed the night before. The wife explained, mid-complaint, that the husband's younger brother had performed these rituals and caused this entanglement. The deceased child connected to this specific

portal turned out to be the same child Bhaiya had seen the previous night, still being held and mourned. Bhaiya describes this as the first time he has ever genuinely felt afraid during such an experience — not from encountering spirits generally , which does not frighten him, but from the sheer intensity of this family's grief and entanglement.
17. Bhaiya's Own Astral Journey , Part Four: Fleeing Without Completing the Rescue

Bhaiya describes feeling his own ener gy draining as he tried to help, without being able to actually resolve the situation — and ultimately , out of fear , leaving the vision without completing what he had been sent to do. He describes this candidly as a personal failure (" मैं भगोड़ा सािबत हो गया" — I turned out to be a deserter/coward), acknowledging he may not yet have been suf ficiently prepared, and states his intention to study further and specifically return to this same case once better equipped, since the family genuinely still needs help.
18. Why Devtas Never Fully Leave Earth or Attain Full Liberation

Bhaiya connects this experience to a broader teaching: devtas never fully abandon earth or seek complete liberation for themselves precisely because of unresolved obligations like this — cases of people in desperate need, praying and pleading, that still require resolution. Repaying such debts (rin) is what continues to earn blessing and grace, which is part of why full liberation is not something devtas actively seek.
19. A Broader Reflection: Karmic Debt Across Two Lifetimes

As a further reflection on unresolved suf fering, Bhaiya references a case where a family lost two children across two dif ferent lifetimes/incarnations, framing this as an example of unusually significant accumulated karmic debt — noting that a single lifetime, even one as consequential as Bhagwan Ram's own incarnation, can carry enormous weight, and two full lifetimes of loss represent something considerably lar ger still.
20. Why "Negativity of Pitru" Is Often the Simplified Public Explanation

Bhaiya explains that when checking for negativity , the underlying situations are frequently far more complex than can be practically explained to a given person — so "negativity of pitru" is often given as a simplified, workable public explanation for what is, underneath, a much more intricate astral entanglement (such as the kind described in his own story above).
21. "Nothing Is Physical" — The Astral World's Primacy

Bhaiya closes this teaching thread with a broader caution: nothing in this world is purely physical — everything ultimately has an astral dimension — and practitioners should not place excessive trust purely in what is visible to the physical eye alone.
22. A Related Case Refer ence: The Double-Coma Tantrik Case

As a further illustration of serious astral-level work, Bhaiya references a specific case involving a woman in a "double coma," which Baba assigned to them. Only three people in India, per this teaching, were specifically appointed by devtas to end a particular tantrik's harmful chain of influence — Bhaiya was one of the three, and together they fully ended that chain within roughly a year and a half.
23. The 1 1-Day Sadhna: Practical Requir ements

For the 1 1-day sadhna specifically , the practical guidance given includes: roughly four hours of jaap; only one diya (lamp) needed for Baba (not two), plus one separate diya kept continuously lit for Kul Devta/Kul Devi; tilak should be applied to Baba's murti using rice (chawal) and flowers (phool), with itr (fragrance) optional; sleeping on the ground is required, though a mattress/gadda placed directly on the floor is acceptable; food should only be eaten after 3:00 AM (practitioners should wake at 3:00 AM), not necessarily waiting for sunrise; no food after 6:00 PM, water only permitted in the evening; if a practitioner splits their practice into two two-hour sessions, the diya should be lit again for the second session.
24. Daily Sharing Is Part of the Practice

Bhaiya specifically instructs this batch to share their daily experiences with him, noting that although he does not normally disclose personal experiences this openly to the wider public, he does so consistently with the Third Eye batch specifically — framing this mutual daily sharing, along with fresh shakti sent daily and daily "meetings," as a core part of this particular sadhna track.
25. The Prayer for New Enrollees

Practitioners newly joining this sadhna are given a simple prayer to repeat: applying tilak to Baba, sitting before Baba, and asking to be included in Bhaiya's sankalp and guru parampara (lineage) — repeating this prayer sincerely and consistently is described as the basis on which new practitioners will be included and prepared for the next stage.
QUICK RULES SUMMARY

This 1 1-day sadhna is a prerequisite stage before further secret sadhnas and havan permission become available. Practitioners gradually discover individual vidya specializations (cell repairing, trikaal drishti, mind-reading, agni vidya, ashwini vidya, sanjivani vidya, and others) — no one masters every vidya, but coordination among dif ferently-specialized practitioners fills the gap. Mastering a healing vidya typically does not extend to healing oneself or one's own family — illustrated by the Akshara/Ankur Bhaiya and Kabir ji/T ulsidas ji examples — because a practitioner's invoked shakti belongs to their purva janam shakti, which pitru (connected only via karmic-debt circumstance) have no authority over . Four astral-world rules given at this level: (1) no single mantra works identically for everyone, but some mantra works for everyone specifically; (2) only your own kundalini shakti and mahasookshma sharir protect you from cosmic entanglement — not even your Gurudev; (3) invoking these shaktis transfers bodily authority away from you, freeing you from ordinary physical anxieties as long as you remain useful to those forces; (4) sincere intentions manifest fully once these shaktis are invoked, including unintended curses — meaning extreme care in speech is required. Praying for others' benefit (rather than one's own) at this level tends to result in receiving the same gift as well — illustrated by Bhaiya's own drishti-opening story . Never proactively of fer spiritual help — only assist once someone genuinely , desperately asks. Bhaiya shared a personally dif ficult account of visiting a realm of deceased children, then being led to a grieving family whose own rituals had opened a direct astral portal into that same realm — he ultimately fled the vision out of fear without completing the rescue, and has committed to returning better prepared. Devtas do not seek full liberation partly because of ongoing unresolved obligations of this kind; "negativity of pitru" is often a simplified public explanation for deeper , more complex astral entanglements. The 1 1-day sadhna's practical rules: ~4 hours of jaap, one diya for Baba plus one continuous diya for Kul Devta/Devi, tilak with rice and flowers, sleeping on the ground (mattress on floor acceptable), eating only after 3:00 AM, no food after 6:00 PM, and daily sharing of experiences with Bhaiya. Spelling note: the institute's name is written "Ashaeiynn" — use this spelling consistently .

Q22. How did this experience differ from Bhaiya's usual encounters with spirits? A: Per this teaching, Bhaiya states he does not normally fear encountering spirits, but felt genuinely afraid for the first time specifically because of the sheer intensity of this family's grief and entanglement.

A: Per this teaching, practitioners are asked to share their daily experiences with Bhaiya, who in turn shares fresh shakti daily and maintains daily contact with this specific batch — a level of ongoing mutual sharing not extended publicly to everyone.

Q30. What prayer ar e new enrollees given for this sadhna? A: Per this teaching, new enrollees are told to apply tilak to Baba, sit before Baba, and sincerely and repeatedly ask to be included in Bhaiya's sankalp and guru parampara (lineage) as the basis for being included and prepared for the next stage.
Bot Response Guidelines

Present the self-healing limitation (healers typically cannot heal themselves or close family) as this teaching's own explanatory framework, tied specifically to the pitru/purva-janam-shakti distinction — do not present it as a universal claim independent of that reasoning. Keep the four "astral world rules" distinct and precise (mantra individuality; kundalini/mahasookshma as sole cosmicentanglement protection; bodily-authority transfer with its usefulness caveat; guaranteed manifestation of sincere intentions including curses) — do not mer ge them into a single generic rule. Present the curse/manifestation rule as an explicit caution about the power of speech and intention at this level, and make clear Bhaiya states he does not actively wish harm on anyone — this is a warning, not an endorsement of cursing others. Preserve Bhaiya's personal astral-journey account (the realm of deceased children, the gatekeepers, the grieving family's portal, and his own admitted fear and incomplete rescue) as his own first-person, unusually candid testimony shared specifically with this batch — not as a resolved, completed case. Keep "negativity of pitru" framed as this teaching's own acknowledged simplification for more complex underlying astral situations, not as a claim that pitru negativity explanations are generally false.

Keep the 1 1-day sadhna's practical rules (diya count, tilak materials, ground-sleeping, eating times) precise and as stated, since these are specific, actionable instructions given to enrolled practitioners.
